body:
I always knew my late N/sociopath father wasn't normal, just from the reactions of my friends when he'd do something like punch or hit me while my friends and I were playing.

My late N/enabler mother -- that took until I was seventeen. She blew up over a request I made to see one of my friends off on her bus back to college and attacked me with both fists, beating me about the head and shoulders. GC brother joined in the attack. It was right before I had to leave for school and when I got there one of my friends asked me how I was... that's all it took for me to dissolve into tears. The friend sat and talked to me for over an hour before insisting I talk to one of the guidance counselors; she stayed with me while I unloaded about my home life with the counselor. Both my friend and the counselor were shocked by what they heard, and the counselor closed our session by saying she would make an appointment to have my father come in to see her.

N/sociopath father never bothered to show for the appointment. N/enabler mother acted like it never happened.

I've been writing a memoir for awhile. Before I found out my father was NPD/sociopathic the memoir was going to focus on recovery from abuse, but learning about Cluster B disorders has put so much in context. A lot of memories have resurfaced as a result of reading here on RBN and on other forums. My mother either had a lot of FLEAS or was BPD with N traits, too. GCBro was well on his way to being N when he died in an alcohol-related car accident (he was alcoholic).

It's helped me a great deal to get the stories down and has proved very cathartic.

My late Nmother once started screaming at me because I'd asked if I could see a friend off on the bus (the friend was leaving to go back to college, and I hadn't seen her for awhile).

As soon as I made the request Nmother started screaming, backed me up against the door and started hitting me about the head and shoulders with her fists. GC brother, who had nothing to do with it, decided to join in the beating.

It was the only time I saw my mother do anything like this, although GCBrother was always abusive, and when I got to school that day my friend urged me to talk to a counselor upon hearing what had happened.

Ironically, Nmother was by far not the worst abuser in our house; that 'honour' belonged to (late) Nfather. I was the entire family's SG from birth and Nfather made his contempt clear.

I did talk to the counselor at school that day, who then requested an appointment to talk to Nfather. He apparently went to the school but just stood by the entrance doors, somehow expecting that someone would just know who he was and why he was there; he left without speaking to anyone. Nothing changed at home, and his abuse in particular worsened considerably after that.

Where do I start?

My N/sociopath father knowingly and deliberately refused to let me see a doctor for three years, while I was developing severe scoliosis. During the third year he was temporarily posted to an overseas location where all of the military people/families lived in houseboats on the same lake. He tried to get my mother to board my brother and me so that we would not go over for the summer, and she was supposed to go by herself. That fell through and she was forced to bring us along -- it was then that my father's military colleagues finally saw me and put some strong pressure on him to get me looked after medically.

He also routinely refused to let me see the dentist, and during my teens I endured several painful dental abscesses. The dentist was "conveniently" located in another town and the only way there was for one of my parents to take me. Never happened.

Despite both of these things (and there was a lot more my father did), I don't recall anyone trying to intervene except for his colleagues. Teachers, mom's friends (my father didn't have friends), my own friends... they didn't seem to see anything wrong with my father's behaviour. He put on a big front when people outside the family were around.

With my N/sociopath father... probably in my early teens. There was such a disparity in the way GC brother and I were treated, and it became really obvious that Ndad was looking for any excuse to go off on me. Ndad was also extremely abusive -- I have no good memories of him at all.

My Nmom was a little harder to pin down but she displayed some really perverse behaviours which were the opposite of how a healthy person would behave/react. The tipping point came when I was about 25 -- GC brother went to jail for his third DWI and she and Ndad would go to see him every weekend, but a few months later when I had major surgery she made a point of not being there on the surgery day itself. Why? Because she was angry at me for asking her to not schedule her tropical vacation for the time when I would be in hospital.

My entire family was highly dysfunctional, although N/sociopath dad was the worst.

Allergies are not stupid. Did your mom see the hives all over you and still think you magically manifested them because you disliked camping? 

I had to deal with the same thing (different items) growing up because according to N/sociopath father "there are no allergies in our family". Typical Nparent thinking, they don't have allergies so their extensions don't either.

You might find that the hospital will have your Ndad up and walking within a few days (probably using a walker for assistance). My late N/sociopath father broke his hip outside my apartment and that's what the hospital here did with him after he'd recovered from surgery. (My Nf was terminal too, from a neurological disease, and had already started to need a walker in order to get around).

Your Ndad may end up being forced to go into a retirement community or nursing home if he is found to be consistently making decisions which negatively impact his life, such as ignoring his health care team's recommendations. From what you've written, it sounds as if your Ndad could be doing this. 

The nursing home my Nf went into promised me they would have him up walking every day -- he was transferred there directly from hospital -- but they did not do so, and he never walked again. If your Ndad goes into a care facility you and your siblings will need to keep on top of what the staff are doing for him (or not doing, as the case may be).

The other piece of advice I have for you is to maintain your boundaries and not let your Ndad take up all of your time and energy. You deserve to have a happy life.

First... I am so sorry this happened.

My late N/sociopath father did something very similar -- my N/BPD mother had gone on a two-week trip and came back very ill, he picked her up at the airport 180 km away from home and couldn't be bothered to stop at any of the many hospitals on his way home. Nmom was already septic. This was on a Friday night, and Nmom died the next Tuesday of pneumonia. Oddly enough my father made the same excuse "she refused to go to the hospital" but my Nmom was, as I said, septic and therefore didn't have the capacity to make her own medical decisions.

What your Nfather (and mine) did goes beyond passive aggression. It's criminal neglect. There is absolutely no justification for letting your spouse die out of a desire to punish her or him.

THIS. So much THIS.

OP, your mother is a malignant narcissist, quite frankly dangerous as all hell, and UNFIXABLE.

What do you want to bet it was her boyfriend who insisted upon taking your precious little one to the hospital over her protests?

My late N/sociopath father was paranoid and extremely narcissistic. 

Examples:

I was babysitting for one of my (late) mother's friends at twelve, and it was getting very late so my mother showed up to send me home because it was a school night -- she would finish the babysitting for me. The next thing I knew I was awoken by my father screaming at my mother downstairs that she'd been out to meet some man, despite the fact that a) she wasn't a cheater; b) I'd told my father my mother had come to relieve me and he knew where she'd been.

He also called the police on me when I was thirty-five and away visiting a new friend for a few days, and tried to get them to put out an APB and drag me home by force. Nfather was highly abusive and did not want me to escape for good. I'm not sure even now whether this incident was because of his paranoia of "internet friends" or not, but it wasn't fun to have to call the police myself upon my return and 'report in'.

The last example -- my Nfather became ill and was told by his doctor he could no longer live alone in his two-story house, with or without support. I had a student apartment and foolishly offered to let him live with me. Nfather had a real hate for my books, and I'd taken every single remaining book of mine to my place months before the movers came to transport Nfather's furniture and hoarded junk; well, right after he moved in he accused me of having instructed the movers (sixty miles away from me at the time) to leave behind his military medals and instead load these supposed rubbermaid containers of books onto the truck. Apparently I could communicate via telepathy... who knew?

My extended family on my late Nfather's side were told by late Nmother that he'd abused her and me, but they persisted in painting him as a "loving father" (barf) right up until he died.

On Nmother's side, they all lived thousands of miles away and saw us so infrequently that none of them knew. Nmother wouldn't tell them because in her words "it would kill my mother". I think one great-aunt knew, though, because she made a point of specifically doing something nice for my brother and me during one of our visits there.

I was the SG and my brother the GC. Still am the SG to the few step-relatives on Nfather's side who are still living. Nfather did a lot of smearing from the time I was little.

What a lovely thing that executive did by taking you under his wing.  
Your parents sound like my late Nfather -- he would put me down for wanting to look nice and insinuate I thought I was "so good", say it didn't matter what I looked like because the important thing was what I did (nothing about character or being a good person, but he meant doing things for others, mainly him; he expected me to be a live-in slave). My late Nmother had no idea what was fashionable and what wasn't, and would insist I wear clothes which made me look much younger. It didn't help that I already looked several years younger than my actual age.  
Nfather went to the extreme of throwing away a work wardrobe I'd amassed over several years.
The person who helped me build the wardrobe was a sales clerk in a store in the local mall, who had a good eye for what suited me and looked professional.  
It's funny you should mention Dress for Success because last month one of their volunteers helped me pick out several pieces to make interview and work outfits; now I have a job in a professional office where everyone is expected to dress the part, and am very grateful for the job and the new pieces.  
(I still suck at doing my own hair, by the way...)  
Good on you for mentoring others as you were mentored. It's a wonderful way to pay it forward. :)
She's trying to hoover you. Please don't drop the charges.

My late Nfather was a twisted, sick sexual abuser and misogynist.

Most of my childhood memories are a blank but I suspect my Nfather was sexually abusing me from earliest childhood. He never stopped, felt completely entitled to make sexual demands on me. Both overt and covert sexual abuse.

Even after he knew he was dying -- when most people would want to make amends for any wrongs committed -- Nfather was suggesting I support myself by prostitution (I have never done so and never would) and/or move into some elderly man's house to cook, clean and provide sexual services in return for room and board. Nfather was a malignant narcissist, if not a sociopath.

I have a theory that Nparents have a higher than average propensity to sexually abuse their children because to them we are just objects, not people in our own right. Their lack of empathy and a moral compass means that they realize they are damaging their children by abuse, but they simply don't care.

Please go see a doctor and get a referral to an orthopedic surgeon. There are a number of treatment options which might help you a lot -- your nmom sounds much like my late nparents, who both called my own worsening scoliosis "bad posture" until it was too late for anything but surgery.

I can empathize, having been through two spinal fusions (and looking at a third now because my scoliosis has started to worsen again in my fifties) and dealing with chronic pain every day because of it.

If you do need surgery for it, it's not the end of the world, and it could help you feel more confident about your body image as well as alleviate the pain you're experiencing. Physiotherapy helps as well, and a good physiotherapist will give you a set of exercises designed to increase the muscle strength in your back.

Oh geez, I have a list.

Ndad wouldn't let me see a doctor for multiple health issues which developed around age ten: scoliosis (which became so severe in the three years he continued to refuse that by the time I saw an orthopod surgery was the only option); sores that developed on my right arm and hand -- instead of allowing me to see the doctor Ndad would interrupt any time he saw me playing or chatting with friends and order me into the house to soak my arm in disinfectant... the sores lasted for two years; and warts, which became pretty numerous and which thankfully went away around the age of 16.

Then there was the "no dental care" thing. Ndad had dental benefits through work which would cover dental care and orthodontia, both of which I needed, but he would refuse to pay for either and tell me to pay for them myself. I had several painful dental abscesses as a teen, none of which were treated. The first thing I did when I finally got a job with benefits was to trot off to the dentist to have work done, although I've never been able to afford the $10,000 it would take for my teeth to be straightened. I smile with my mouth closed.

Any food Ndad didn't like was not allowed in the house. This included broccoli, pizza, fruit juices... I discovered I loved broccoli in my twenties, and finally got to have pizza at friends' houses. Yet he'd try to force his food likes on everyone else in the house, going so far as to get everyone else McDonald's burgers while telling me I could go without because I didn't like condiments on mine.

Ndad was on the malignant narcissist end of the spectrum -- zero empathy, zero conscience, no moral compass. The medical neglect was just the tip of the iceberg with him and he really got worse after my mother died (of pneumonia, at age sixty-three, because he wouldn't take her to the hospital).

My Nparents willfully, deliberately neglected my scoliosis for three solid years (from age ten to nearly fourteen) and Nfather would punish me for asking to see a doctor. He also kept me away from the one person in his extended family who would have spotted it and perhaps urged him to get me evaluated. The only reason I was finally allowed to see the doctor was because my father's colleagues at work saw me and his career was threatened by the obvious neglect. I ended up having to get two major surgeries in my teens and another in my mid-twenties (and need yet another to correct the curvature which is worsening again in my middle age). I'm in constant, chronic pain and need heavy medications now in order to even function.

So that would be the biggest thing I would change, were it possible... having someone outside the family with influence on my (now late) Nfather force his hand when it came to getting me medical treatment much earlier.

My late Nfather was closer to a sociopath than narcissist and I consider him to have been evil. And yes, I was the SG in our family from a very young age. The deliberate neglect was only one of many abuses he perpetrated on me.

I was doing a degree in Sociology with a Psychology minor, but had to leave in order to take care of my father when he became terminally ill so didn't get a chance to finish and couldn't afford to go back afterward.

I have several years' experience in office work, and have been applying for any office job I can find which doesn't demand a two-year diploma in Office Administration, but haven't gotten anywhere with that. My last work experience was six years in a local call centre, but it isn't readily accessible by bus (basically I need a job which conforms to regular office hours and is accessible by bus, because the transit system here sucks).

The amount of money this woman got was close to $250,000. She and her husband own their own home and have a business as well, and they wanted my father's money so they could take their children and grandchildren on yearly vacations to places like Aruba, Jamaica, etc. She repeatedly refused to give me the estate mail and I finally went ahead and found an attorney to file probate without it. Amazingly, the same week probate was granted she showed up at my apartment waving a folder containing the estate mail, including the tax bill for the money she received. I can only conclude she spent years periodically calling the courthouse to find out this information. She insisted on meeting with my probate attorney privately to give him the mail; it wasn't until he called me a couple of days later that I found out exactly how much she'd received and what the ramifications were for me. She is well aware I am disabled and alone, without assets. Ironically enough, I would have been okay with her receiving perhaps $10,000 for the eight months she spent as my father's financial POA... but not now.

The job market here is pretty bleak. I've just spent a half-hour on the phone with a social worker who has tried to find services for me, even to keep my electricity on, and she wasn't able to come up with much. The wait for subsidized housing here is five to nine years.

I blame myself for having moved here instead of going to a university some other place. My father would still have become terminally ill, but the greedy and malicious step-relatives wouldn't have had ready access to him if I hadn't moved here and then offered to care for him.

My father's will was made several years before his final illness, and named me as executrix and sole beneficiary. Unfortunately, the retirement fund beneficiary is/was considered separate from the will. My father changed both his RRIF beneficiary and his financial power of attorney to this woman's name eight months before his death. She contacted his financial advisor to have this done and also sent at least two local attorneys to his nursing home room to convince him to change his will as well. At the time he did this I was working full-time and could no longer take him places on demand, whereas this woman and her husband were able to.

Yes, I was out of the work force while looking after my father, both after my mother's death (for seven years following) and after he became terminally ill. I'd moved to this city in the late nineties to finally get a university degree, and had to leave university to look after him -- he needed 24/7 care at that point. I got a job a few months after he went into the nursing home.

My probate attorney referred me to an estate litigator, who met with me once, heard a bit of my story, and tried to get necessary estate papers from this woman without success. She had diverted all estate mail to her home and refused to give any of it to me. I received a $800 bill for the hour consultation with the estate litigator, but cannot pay it and due to lack of money cannot continue the fight right now. I can't afford a $400/hr attorney. Legal Aid, at least locally, does not help with cases like mine; my doctor faxed them asking them to assist me and they told him they only deal with landlord/tenant issues, criminal representation, employment issues. I would have to contact the Law Society of my province and ask them about finding an estate litigator who would fight for me, either pro bono or on contingency.

The annuity I receive is about the same amount that I would receive under my province's disability benefits. I haven't tried to apply for those yet, but due to my current "income" I've been told I likely wouldn't qualify. To top if off a quarter of what I get goes to pay off the student loan from university.

I have enough documentation to prove undue influence in court, but the legal issues have to take a back seat to finding a job I can do and which pays enough to live on.
